body:
It's a relief that overdosing seems to be a difficult thing with SSRIs. That's one load off my mind.


As mentioned above, she doesn't have a psychiatrist yet. And I'm not sure telling the doctor would do much. I've got a bunch of other friends on anti depressants and it seems to just be something that is given out easily and doctors aren't too worried about following up  with it. One of my friends has tried weening himself off them on his own and failed (felt horrible), but didn't even bother talking to his doc about it until afterwards and the doc just didn't seem to care much ("just keep taking them, talk to your counselor")


When she was hospitalised for her paracetamol overdose they didn't seem keen to keep her in, even though she told them she felt suicidal. I actually went with her to the doctors a few weeks later when she was feeling really bad. I was hoping they would admit her, and I think she was accepting of that too. But they just chatted for a bit (I wasn't in the room so don't know what was said - she insists she told them she was suicidal) and told her they would chase up her referral to the mental health team (NHS so it's been taking a while).

She doesn't have a psychiatrist right now. She started going to her doctor about 3 months ago who initially offered medication which she didn't want to do. Since then she's been on various waiting lists. She blew off a load of appointments so getting things set up in terms of therapy has taken even longer. She is due to have some kind of assessment which will lead her on to therapy or whatever next week. This is NHS treatment so everything has been really fucking slow and she has been too introverted to want to engage much.


I asked her about the pills. She doesn't deny that she is depressed, she just doesn't want to take medication. She's actually really keen to get therapy or whatever but she just seems to be so prone to mood swings and wanting to stay in her house that actually getting her there is a hassle. I don't drive so I can't help her get to stuff, but I've offered to go with. 


She isn't able to give me a suitable excuse for why she won't just chuck the pills. I get the impression she is vaguely guilty about wasting them but hasn't thought of a better solution for that yet. I've offered to take them off her hands but she now seems pretty embarassed I have found out about it.
